title: Hruso language - Wikipedia
text: Hruso, also known as Aka (Angka), is a language of Arunachal Pradesh India. Long assumed to be a Sino-Tibetan language, it may actually be a language isolate. [2][3] It is spoken by 3,000 people in 21 villages in Thrizino Circle, West Kameng District. [2]

title: Tibeto-Burman languages - Wikipedia
text: The remaining languages of Arunachal Pradesh are much more diverse, belonging to the small Siangic, Kho-Bwa (or Kamengic), Hruso, Miju and Digaro languages (or Mishmic) groups. [26] These groups have relatively little Tibeto-Burman vocabulary, and Bench and Post dispute their inclusion in Sino-Tibetan. [27]

title: Sino-Tibetan Branches Project (STBP) by Andy Hsiu - Hruso-Miji
text: The Hruso-Miji and Kho-Bwa branches are likely very early Eastern Sino-Tibetan splits that have undergone influences from non-Sino-Tibetan languages. Hruso is one of the most lexically divergent languages, and show the most evidence of likely influence from non-Sino-Tibetan languages.

title: Hruso | Ethnologue Free
text: Hruso is an endangered indigenous language of India. It belongs to the Sino-Tibetan language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people. It is not known to be taught in schools.
